name: Sandpiper Bay
title: Artificial Turf in Sandpiper Bay, NC | TIMELESS Grass & Greens
description: Sandpiper Bay's covenants ban artificial vegetation outright and bar fences and dog runs. Get the ARC's written answer before you plan turf or a pet area.
h1: Artificial turf in Sandpiper Bay, NC, planned around the covenants and the ARC.
lede: Before you pay for a design, get the ARC's written answer on whether turf counts as the artificial vegetation the covenants ban. Then we draw a layout you approve.
wins: Get the ARC's written answer on artificial vegetation first
A layout that needs no fence and no dog run
Turf area in square feet, ready for the ARC's 60-day review

answer.question: Does Sandpiper Bay's HOA allow artificial turf?
answer.answer: Unclear, so ask. The covenants ban artificial vegetation outdoors but don't name turf or define the term. Any landscaping change also needs ARC approval, which can be refused on looks alone. Get the ARC's answer in writing first.

blocks.h2: Section 25 bans "artificial vegetation." Nobody has told us if that means turf.
blocks.takeaway: The covenants ban artificial vegetation on any lot's exterior, but neither they nor the HOA's summary define the term or name turf. Put that question to the ARC in writing before any layout is drawn.
paras: Sandpiper Bay's Declaration of Protective Covenants, revised May 2, 2016, is direct in Article II, Section 25: "No artificial vegetation shall be permitted on the exterior of any portion of the Subdivision." The same section allows exterior sculpture, fountains and flags with prior Association or ARC approval, and protects the display of the American flag. Turf is not named on either side of that sentence.

The HOA's own plain-English summary, dated February 23, 2026, restates it under "What's Not Allowed": "Artificial plants outdoors." That's a resident-written gloss on the covenant, not a new rule, and it doesn't settle whether turf grass reads the same as artificial plants. Neither document was written with synthetic turf in mind.

That gap is the whole decision. We don't guess at it and neither should you. Before any layout is drawn, put Section 25 in front of the Architectural Review Committee and ask, in writing, whether it treats turf as artificial vegetation. If the answer is no, keep that letter with your ARC application. If it's yes, you'll know before paying for a design instead of after.

blocks.kicker: No fence, no dog house, no run
blocks.h2: A new rule bars fences and animal runs outright — plan pet turf without one.
blocks.takeaway: The covenants bar fences, dog houses and animal runs outright, with no exception for pets. We lay out a pet area inside your property lines and any approved screening, with no fence in the plan.
paras: Article II carries a section labeled "New Section 4" in the recorded document: "No fences, walls, above ground pools, dog houses, animal pens or animal runs shall be constructed on any Lot. No hedge, shrubbery or vegetation of any kind shall be grown or placed in the form of a fence or wall on any Lot except used as a privacy screen according to ARC Guidelines." It doesn't carve out dog owners.

That matters for pet turf specifically. A fenced run is the usual way to keep a dog area contained, and Sandpiper Bay's covenants remove that option along with the dog house itself. Exhibit B's setback table, which once listed a fence setback for lots backing the golf course, has that line struck through in the recorded copy — consistent with the fence ban rather than in conflict with it.

If you want a defined pet area, we lay it out inside your existing property lines and any approved landscape screening, with no fence or structure in the plan. Our Grand Strand pet turf page covers drainage and pet waste in a fenceless yard.

blocks.h2: Any exterior change needs a decision — and the ARC can say no on looks alone.
blocks.takeaway: Swapping a lawn for turf is a landscaping change that needs ARC approval, which can be refused on looks alone. The ARC has 60 days to decide on complete plans, or they're deemed approved.
paras: Article VIII of the covenants gives the Architectural Review Committee "exclusive jurisdiction over all construction on any portion of the Subdivision," a category that explicitly includes plantings and removal of plants. "Any change in exterior appearance of any building, wall, fence or other structural improvements, and any change in the appearance of the landscaping, shall be deemed an alteration requiring approval." Digging out a lawn and laying turf is a landscaping change under that language.

The ARC has 60 days after you submit complete plans and specifications to approve or disapprove; if it misses that window, the application is deemed approved. But the covenant also gives it wide latitude going the other way: "Refusal of approval of plans, specifications, and plot plans or any of them may be based on any grounds, including purely aesthetic grounds, which in the sole and uncontrolled discretion of the ARC may seem sufficient." A clean written scope, with the Section 25 question already answered, gives you the clearest shot at a fast yes.

The Board proposed streamlining this process in an October 2020 written ballot to owners, which would have split review into a 30-day ARC recommendation and a 15-day Board sign-off. That ballot needed 67% owner approval; we found no record confirming it passed, so ask the HOA's management company which version of Article VIII governs your application today.

blocks.h2: Water has to go somewhere the Association already approved.
blocks.takeaway: If a turf base would shift where your lot's water drains, the Association and ARC must approve a drainage plan first. On course lots, patios, decks and pools stay 20 feet off the course line.
paras: Article II, Section 24 covers drainage directly: "No Owner shall modify, change, channel or direct drainage water onto a neighboring Lot, Common Area or the Golf Course except in accordance with a drainage plan approved by the Association and the ARC and in the case of drainage onto the Golf Course, the owner of the Golf Course." A turf base changes how a yard sheds water, so if your lot's drainage pattern would shift, that plan needs sign-off before we grade.

Lots that back the golf course carry their own setbacks under the covenants' Exhibit B: residences stay 30 feet off the course line, and patios, decks, pools and similar features stay 20 feet off it. Interior lots not abutting the course keep a 20-foot rear setback. We measure your lot against whichever line applies before the layout is drawn, so the turf edge lands inside it.

blocks.h2: The 2016 covenants describe Phase I. Check that your lot is in it.
blocks.takeaway: These covenants cover Lots 1 through 70 of the platted subdivision — Cape Side and Wyndfall aren't part of it. Ask the HOA's management office which rules apply to your lot first.
paras: The recorded covenants' Exhibit A describes the property they cover as Lots 1 through 70 of "Sandpiper Bay Golf Plantation PUD," per two 1998 survey plats recorded in Brunswick County. The Town of Sunset Beach's own mosquito-control schedule names Sandpiper Bay, Cape Side and Wyndfall on the same Monday spray route — evidence the Town services all three, though a shared spray route doesn't by itself establish that any of them sits inside the Town's corporate limits. Cape Side and Wyndfall aren't part of the platted Sandpiper Bay lots this declaration covers, so the Section 25 and fence rules above are Sandpiper Bay's, not automatically theirs. If your lot is in Cape Side or Wyndfall, or falls outside the platted Phase I lots, ask the HOA's management office which declaration, if any, actually applies to your property before you rely on anything in this page.

Whether a Town of Sunset Beach permit applies here, on top of the ARC's review, depends on Sandpiper Bay's actual jurisdictional status, which we haven't confirmed against a boundary map or the Town's own statement. Ask the Town's permitting office directly before you plan around it; our Sunset Beach page covers the Town's stormwater and Fill and Grade permit rules if they apply. At the free visit, we measure the yard, check where water sits after rain, and put the turf area in writing so you can take one square-footage figure to whichever offices need it.

servicesNote: A lawn, a fenceless pet area or a backyard green — each one built to fit inside a covenant that bans fences and asks the ARC's opinion on synthetic materials.

faq.q: Does artificial turf count as "artificial vegetation" under Section 25?
faq.a: Neither the covenants nor the HOA's plain-English summary defines the term, and we found no ARC ruling on file. Ask the Architectural Review Committee in writing before you commit to a design, and keep its answer with your application.

faq.q: Can I fence a small area for turf and a dog?
faq.a: The covenants' New Section 4 bars fences, dog houses, animal pens and animal runs on any lot outright, with no pet exception. Plan a pet turf layout without a fence, using property lines and any ARC-approved screening instead.

faq.q: How long does ARC approval take?
faq.a: Under the recorded 2016 language, the ARC has 60 days after receiving complete plans to approve or disapprove; no response in that window counts as approval. A 2020 proposal to shorten that process needed a 67% owner vote and we found no confirmation it passed, so confirm the current timeline with the HOA's management company.

faq.q: Does my lot's turf plan need Town of Sunset Beach permits too?
faq.a: Possibly, on top of ARC approval. The Town of Sunset Beach sprays Sandpiper Bay directly under its mosquito-control schedule, which shows the Town services the community, but that doesn't by itself confirm the neighborhood sits inside town limits or under Town permitting jurisdiction. Ask the Town's permitting office whether its stormwater and grading rules, covered on our Sunset Beach town page, apply to your lot, and take the same square-footage figure to whichever offices need it.
